finding: Chicago’s grid of main streets continues past the city limit, but frequent bus and train service mostly does not. Among square miles with 5,000 to 10,000 residents, half of those in Chicago get 10.9 or more buses and trains an hour, while half of those in the suburbs get 1.4 or fewer. A bus or train comes at least every 15 minutes for 94% of Chicago residents, but for only 12% of people in the suburbs.

ledger.source: CTA, Metra and Pace GTFS schedules
ledger.units: 8,445,866 residents (2020 Census) in 141,168 blocks of six counties; 2,896 square miles
method: Weekday service of Tuesday 10 November 2026, 7:00–19:00: per route, departures an hour at its busiest stop within ¼ mi (bus) or ½ mi (rail), summed
Square miles of Chicago’s address grid, extended past the city limit; service weighted by residents
Frequent: 4 or more buses and trains an hour each way; edge drawn on a 0.1 mi lattice, islands and holes under 0.5 sq mi left out
caveats: Straight-line distance to a stop, not the walk
Pace On Demand and Dial-a-Ride are booked services, not schedules, and are not counted; Indiana and Wisconsin are outside the six counties
